chunks: Ja'far ibn Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abdullah ibn al-Mughira al-Kufi (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My grandfather al-Hasan ibn Ali narrated to me, from his grandfather Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Isma'il ibn Muslim, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah's blessings be upon him and his family) said:
Whoever finds a crumb or a date and eats it, it will not leave his stomach until Allah forgives him.

key_terms.تمرة: A single date; dates were a staple food in early Arabian society
key_terms.كسرة: A crumb or broken piece of bread; refers to even the smallest portion of food
key_terms.يغفر: Forgives; divine forgiveness granted as a reward for not wasting food

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for eating a crumb or date found on the ground in Islam?
ai.summary: The Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) taught that even the act of eating a small morsel of food that one finds — whether a crumb of bread or a single date — carries divine reward and forgiveness. This hadith, transmitted through the Imams of Ahl al-Bayt, was delivered in the context of early Muslim society where food scarcity was common and wasting even the smallest amount was viewed as ingratitude toward God's provision.

en.bilal-muhammad: Ja`far b. `Ali b. al-Hasan b. `Ali b. `Abdullah b. al-Mughira al-Kufi (ra) narrated to us. He said: My randfather al-Hasan b. `Ali narrated to me from his grandfather `Abdullah b. al-Mughira from Isma`il b. Muslim from al-Sadiq Ja`far b. Muhammad from his father from his forefathers (as). He said: The Messenger of Allah (s) said:
Whoever finds a crumb or a date and eats it, it will not leave his stomach until Allah forgives him.
